raw_response:
I will keep my farm simple and steady this year. I am 65, I have farmed a long time, and with some family members working off-farm, I will not spread labor too thin. My main income and food-security base is still the wheat-maize rotation, so I will put most of my 10.1 mu into that system and keep only a smaller cotton area. I have well irrigation, so I will use that to protect wheat at key stages and to make sure summer maize establishes well if rainfall is uneven. For wheat, I will use improved seed, moderate-to-high nitrogen, enough phosphorus, some potassium, and a few irrigations because stable grain yield matters most to me. For summer maize, I will use hybrid seed because it is dependable on my land and fits the rotation after wheat; I will fertilize it well but not excessively, and I will irrigate when needed for emergence and grain filling. Cotton takes more field management and picking labor, so I will keep it on a smaller area, use improved seed, fertilize it moderately, irrigate several times from bud stage onward, and control insects carefully because that is where cotton can easily lose yield. I will mostly use rotary tillage because it is practical, familiar, and saves labor compared with deeper ploughing every time.
